summary: This document recommends editorial changes to the IANA IS-IS TLV Codepoints registry so it better reflects the state of the protocol. It also sets guidelines for Designated Experts who review allocations.

eli5.summary: A phone book gets out of date and needs tidying. This RFC cleans up the list of numbered fields that IS-IS uses and tells reviewers how to approve new ones.

questions: what is the is-is tlv codepoints registry
how do designated experts allocate is-is codepoints early
what is expert review in iana
subtitle: Tidies two IS-IS sub-TLV registries and tells Designated Experts when they may allocate codepoints early.

tldr.problem: The IANA IS-IS TLV Codepoints registry did not clearly show how sub-TLVs are shared among TLVs, and there was no registry-specific guidance for allocating codepoints to drafts before they become RFCs.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC merges the prefix reachability sub-TLV registries into one, extends the IS neighbor sub-TLV registry to two more TLVs, and gives six rules for Designated Experts.
tldr.outcome: The protocol itself does not change. Experts can now approve early allocations for documents with Working Group or AD backing.

today: RFC 7370 is a Proposed Standard and has been updated by RFC 9352. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Why the Registry Needed Changes
sections.content:
The IS-IS TLV Codepoints registry was created by RFC 3563 and extended by RFC 6233. Its assignment policy is Expert Review, as defined in RFC 5226: Designated Experts review the codepoints a protocol extension needs before IANA adds them.

Two problems motivated this document. Prefix advertisement TLVs each had their own separate sub-TLV registry, which should be combined as was already done for neighbor advertisement TLVs. And sometimes codepoints from Internet-Drafts that seem likely to gain Working Group approval are needed before those drafts become RFCs.
sections.eli5: The list of numbered fields had grown messy, and reviewers had no clear rules for approving a new field early. This RFC fixes both.

sections.title: The Two Sub-TLV Registries
sections.content:
An existing common registry named "Sub-TLVs for TLVs 22, 141, and 222" covered IS neighbor TLVs. RFC 5311 defines the IS Neighbor Attribute TLV (23) and the MT IS Neighbor Attribute TLV (223), whose formats are identical to TLVs 22 and 222. The registry was extended to include them, with identical inclusion settings, and renamed "Sub-TLVs for TLVs 22, 23, 141, 222, and 223".

For prefix reachability, separate sub-TLV registries previously existed for TLVs 135, 235, 236 and 237. Because sub-TLV assignments were already common to all of them, they were combined into one registry, "Sub-TLVs for TLVs 135, 235, 236, and 237". The RFC stresses this is no change to the protocol, only a clearer representation. The registry currently lists type 1 (32-bit Administrative Tag Sub-TLV) and type 2 (64-bit Administrative Tag Sub-TLV), both from RFC 5130 and valid for all four TLVs. Type 0 and types 3 to 255 are unassigned.
sections.eli5: Several lists that always said the same thing were joined into one list, so nobody has to check four places any more.

sections.title: Guidance for Designated Experts
sections.content:
Early allocation under RFC 7120 does not apply to Expert Review registries. Instead, a request goes to the Designated Experts, who MAY approve it under the registry's guidance. Six rules apply to the IS-IS TLV Codepoints registry.

  • Requests MAY be made at any time.
  • Experts SHOULD only consider requests from drafts already accepted as Working Group documents, or planned as AD Sponsored documents when no suitable Working Group exists.
  • For Working Group documents, experts SHOULD check with the chairs that there is consensus to allocate now. For AD Sponsored documents, they SHOULD check with the AD.
  • Experts SHOULD review the technical merit. They SHOULD NOT overrule IETF consensus but MAY raise issues first.
  • After approval, IANA marks the codepoints with a reference to the document as normal.
  • If the document never becomes an RFC, the expiry and deallocation process of RFC 7120 MUST be followed, with the Designated Experts taking the role of the Working Group chairs.
sections.eli5: Reviewers may say yes early, but only to ideas that a real team has already accepted. If the idea is dropped, they take the number back.

sections.title: IANA Actions and Security
sections.content: IANA has renamed the neighbor sub-TLV registry to "Sub-TLVs for TLVs 22, 23, 141, 222, and 223" and combined the prefix sub-TLV registries for TLVs 135, 235, 236 and 237 into one. The document otherwise provides guidance to the Designated Experts who manage allocation requests.
sections.eli5: IANA, the keeper of the lists, made the name changes and joined the lists.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The Security Considerations section is a single sentence: the document introduces no new security issues. That fits its scope, since it renames and merges registries and sets review guidance without changing any IS-IS message format.
sections.eli5: Nothing here makes anything less safe, because only the lists were tidied.

sections.title: What Changes in Practice
sections.content: For implementers, nothing on the wire changes: existing sub-TLV assignments were already common to all the TLVs sharing a registry. For people writing new IS-IS extensions, the practical change is the path in Section 4. A draft backed by a Working Group, or planned as AD Sponsored, can get codepoints from the Designated Experts without waiting to be published as an RFC.
sections.eli5: The numbered fields stay the same. The only new thing is a faster, fair way to get a new number.
